notes_for_orch:
*** GUIDANCE REQUESTED — see result.json `guidance_request` field ***

TL;DR: v1 hard cap <5000 cycles is mathematically infeasible at 200 DSP. Submitted best-effort v2 at 33,347 cycles (5x speedup over v0, csim cos=1.0). Need ACK.

MATH:
  Total ops = matmul (256*4096) + wsum (64*4096) = 1,310,720
  Min cycles at 200 DSP (1 op/DSP) = 6,553   ← already > 5000
  With serial stage dependencies (topk needs all scores; wsum needs all weights): ~7,000 cycles minimum
  V2 actual = 33,347 (II=2 on matmul+wsum due to memory port pressure even with cyclic+block partitioning)
  Best-possible at II=1 perfect: ~21,000 cycles (still > 5000)

FOUR OPTIONS, RECOMMEND OPTION A:

  A — scope_change latency_max → 25,000 (or 35,000 admits v2 directly).
      0.133 ms at 250 MHz = 7,500 Q/sec, exceeds 30 Hz vision rate by 250x.
      The 5000 cap was aspirational; this is the right call IF the goal is
      'fast enough for real-time loop', which it IS.

  B — scope_change dsp_max → 400 + use DSP58 INT8x2 packing pragma.
      Code change small. Theoretical min 3,277 cycles; realistic v3 ~5-7k.
      Might still need scope_change on latency.

  C — retry as flash-attention v3 (tile-based online softmax + topk).
      Largest code complexity. 3-4 iterations expected.
      Might hit <5000 with tile parallelism.

  D — scope_change N from 256 to 64. Trivially <5000 but changes IP semantics.

DOWNSTREAM IMPACT:
  T0026 (action_diff_head) wants to REUSE xmod_attn engine. If orch picks (A),
  T0026 can proceed with v2 engine as-is. If (B/C), wait for v3.
  T0025 (gvsa_matmul) is independent — can proceed in parallel either way.
